extracted.intended_audience: U.S. patent examiners (and patent practitioners referencing examiner form paragraphs)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and standardized form paragraphs for making and documenting rejections under the various pre‑ and post‑AIA versions of 35 U.S.C. 102 (anticipation/prior art, public use/on sale, applicant not inventor, priority disputes, and related provisional rejections). Includes instructions on when to apply particular statutory paragraphs and required supporting explanations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pre-AIA 35 U.S.C. 102(e) — Patent Application Publication or Patent to Another with Earlier Filing Date (7.12.fti)
rubrics_metrics.description: Use when the invention was described in (1) an application published under 122(b) by another filed in the U.S. before the applicant's invention, or (2) a patent granted on an application by another filed in the U.S. before the applicant's invention; international applications under section 351(a) have the effects of a U.S. application only if they designated the U.S. and were published under PCT Article 21(2) in English.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Only use if reference is (a) a U.S. patent or U.S. application publication filed under 111(a), (b) a U.S. patent issued from, or a U.S./WIPO publication of, an international application with an international filing date on/after Nov 29, 2000, or (c) a U.S. patent from, or WIPO publication of, an international design application that designates the U.S. Consider benefit claims under 119(e), 120, 121, 365(c), 386(c) if subject matter is supported in the earlier application. To rely on an international filing date under pre-AIA 102(e), the PCT must be filed on/after Nov 29, 2000, designate the U.S., and be published in English by WIPO; if not met, treat the reference under 102(a) or (b) as of publication date (see form paragraphs 7.08.fti and 7.09.fti). Precede this paragraph with 7.07.fti (and as appropriate 7.08.fti–7.11.fti).

rubrics_metrics.name: Pre‑AIPA 35 U.S.C. 102(e) — U.S. Patent Issued From International Application Filed Before Nov 29, 2000 (7.12.01.fti)
rubrics_metrics.description: When the reference is a U.S. patent issued (directly or indirectly) from an international application having an international filing date prior to Nov 29, 2000, the changes made by AIPA/2002 do not apply and the prior art date is determined under pre‑AIPA 35 U.S.C. 102(e).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use only if reference is a U.S. patent issued from a national stage or continuing application claiming benefit to an international application with an international filing date prior to Nov 29, 2000. If the reference issued from a national stage, the pre‑AIPA 102(e) date is when requirements of 371(c)(1),(2),(4) were fulfilled. Consider benefit claims under 119(e), 120, 121, 365(c), 386(c) only if the relied‑upon subject matter is appropriately supported. Do NOT consider foreign priority claims under 119(a)–(d), 365(a)/(b), or 386(a)/(b). Precede with 7.07.fti and optionally 7.08.fti–7.11.fti.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pre-AIA 35 U.S.C. 102(f) — Applicant Not the Inventor (7.13.fti)
rubrics_metrics.description: Use when the statutory basis is that the applicant did not themselves invent the subject matter sought to be patented (35 U.S.C. 102(f)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This form paragraph must be preceded by form paragraph 7.07.fti and may be preceded by form paragraphs 7.08.fti to 7.12.fti.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pre-AIA/AIA 35 U.S.C. 102(g) — Priority of Invention (7.14.aia / 7.14.fti)
rubrics_metrics.description: Rejection based on another inventor establishing in an interference (or prior invention in this country) that the other inventor made the invention earlier and did not abandon, suppress, or conceal it; priority determination considers conception dates, reductions to practice, and reasonable diligence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For AIA situations, use 7.14.aia (must be preceded by 7.07.aia). For pre‑AIA use 7.14.fti (precede with 7.07.fti and optionally 7.08.fti–7.13.fti). Note: A 102(g) rejection is appropriate in applications/patents examined under first‑to‑file if they contain claims with effective filing dates before March 16, 2013 or specific 120/121/365(c) references to patents/applications that contain such claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rejection under 35 U.S.C. 102(a)(1)/102(a)(2) (7.15.aia)
rubrics_metrics.description: Form paragraph for rejecting claim(s) under 35 U.S.C. 102 (a)(1) or (a)(2) as being anticipated by prior art.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use only for applications filed on/after March 16, 2013 examined under AIA; must be preceded by 7.03.aia. Insert claim numbers in bracket 1; insert '(a)(1)' or '(a)(2)' in bracket 2 (or both); bracket 3 indicates 'clearly anticipated' or 'anticipated' with explanation; bracket 4 lists prior art relied upon. If (a)(2) applies, use the more specific subparagraph form paragraphs (7.15.01.aia, 7.15.02.aia, or 7.15.03.aia) as applicable. Precede with 7.07.aia and as appropriate 7.08.aia and 7.12.aia, or use form paragraph 7.103. For claims claiming priority/benefit to pre‑March 16, 2013 applications, precede with 7.06.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rejection under pre‑AIA 35 U.S.C. 102(a)/(b) and (g) (7.15.fti)
rubrics_metrics.description: Form paragraph template for rejecting claims under pre‑AIA 35 U.S.C. 102(a), 102(b) (patent or publication), and 102(g).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Insert appropriate paragraph letter(s) of pre‑AIA 102 in bracket 2; indicate 'clearly anticipated' or 'anticipated' in bracket 3 and cite prior art in bracket 4. Precede by 7.07.fti and 7.08.fti/7.09.fti/7.14.fti as appropriate, or by 7.103. If pre‑AIA 102(e) is also applied, follow with one of 7.15.01.fti–7.15.03.fti. For applications with actual filing dates on/after March 16, 2013 that claim priority to pre‑March 16, 2013 filings, precede with 7.06.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provisional Rejection under 35 U.S.C. 102(a)(2) — common assignee/applicant/joint inventor (7.15.01.aia)
rubrics_metrics.description: Provisional rejection of claims under 35 U.S.C. 102(a)(2) as anticipated by a copending application that has a common assignee/applicant or at least one joint inventor and an earlier effective filing date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used in applications filed on/after March 16, 2013 (precede with 7.03.aia). The provisional rejection is based on presumption of future publication/patenting of the copending app. May be overcome by (1) showing under 37 CFR 1.130(a) that the disclosure was obtained from the inventor/joint inventor (not prior art), (2) showing under 37 CFR 1.130(b) of prior public disclosure under 102(b)(2)(B), or (3) statement under 35 U.S.C. 102(b)(2)(C) establishing ownership/assignment/joint research agreement as of the effective filing date. Terminal disclaimer does not overcome this rejection (In re Bartfeld). If claims would be obvious over the copending app, use obviousness form paragraph 7.21.01.aia. Insert required bracket items for claim numbers and application number and explanations of anticipation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provisional Rejection under pre‑AIA 35 U.S.C. 102(e) — common assignee/applicant/joint inventor (7.15.01.fti)
rubrics_metrics.description: Provisional rejection under pre‑AIA 35 U.S.C. 102(e) when a copending application with earlier effective U.S. filing date (common assignee/applicant/joint inventor) discloses the claimed invention but has not yet been published under 122.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Based on presumption of future publication/patenting of the copending application. May be overcome by showing under 37 CFR 1.132 that any invention disclosed but not claimed in the copending app was derived from the inventor of this application (not 'by another'), or by appropriate showing under 37 CFR 1.131(a). Terminal disclaimer does not overcome this rejection. Use form paragraph 7.12.fti to determine copending application's pre‑AIA 102(e) date unless the copending app stems from an international application filed before Nov 29, 2000 (then use 7.12.01.fti). If claims are directed to same invention, make provisional double patenting rejection using form paragraphs 8.30 and 8.32.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rejection under 35 U.S.C. 102(a)(2) — common assignee/applicant/joint inventor (7.15.02.aia)
rubrics_metrics.description: Reject claims under 35 U.S.C. 102(a)(2) as anticipated by a U.S. patent, U.S. patent application publication, or WIPO publication with an earlier effectively filed date that has a common assignee/applicant or at least one common joint inventor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used for applications filed on/after March 16, 2013 (precede with 7.03.aia and 7.12.aia). May be overcome by (1) 37 CFR 1.130(a) showing the subject matter was obtained from the inventor/joint inventor (not prior art), (2) 37 CFR 1.130(b) showing prior public disclosure under 102(b)(2)(B) if same invention not being claimed, or (3) statement under 35 U.S.C. 102(b)(2)(C) establishing common ownership/assignment/joint research agreement as of effective filing date. If copending claims are to the same invention, make provisional double patenting rejection (8.30/8.32) and require cancellation/amendment of patentably indistinct claims (8.27.aia).

rubrics_metrics.name: Rejection under pre‑AIA 35 U.S.C. 102(e) — common assignee/applicant/joint inventor (7.15.02.fti)
rubrics_metrics.description: Reject claims under pre‑AIA 35 U.S.C. 102(e) as anticipated by a patent or patent application publication with an earlier effective filing date that has common assignee/applicant or a common joint inventor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use pre‑AIA 102(e) as amended by AIPA/2002 (form paragraph 7.12.fti) to determine the reference's 102(e) date unless the reference stems from an international application filed before Nov 29, 2000 (then use 7.12.01.fti). May be overcome by a showing under 37 CFR 1.132 that any disclosed-but-unclaimed invention was derived from the same inventive entity, or by 37 CFR 1.131(a) if the same invention is not being claimed. Consider benefit claims under 119(e), 120, 121, 365(c), 386(c) only if supported. Do not consider foreign priority claims under 119(a)–(d), etc. Patent application publications may be used only if preceded by 7.12.fti.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rejection under pre‑AIA 35 U.S.C. 102(e) — no common assignee or inventor(s) (7.15.03.fti)
rubrics_metrics.description: Reject claims under pre‑AIA 35 U.S.C. 102(e) as anticipated by a patent or patent application publication with an earlier filing date where the reference need not have a common assignee or inventor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use when reference is a patent or patent application publication with earlier filing date; apply 7.12.fti or 7.12.01.fti as appropriate to determine 102(e) date. If a PCT publication has international filing date prior to Nov 29, 2000 and did not designate the U.S. or was not published in English by WIPO, do not use this paragraph and treat the reference as prior art under 102(a) or (b) as of publication date (see 7.08.fti/7.09.fti). Insert 'clearly anticipated' or 'anticipated' with explanation and cite prior art; patent application publications may be used only if 7.12.fti preceded this paragraph.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rejection under 35 U.S.C. 102(a)(2) — no common assignee or inventor(s) (7.15.03.aia)
rubrics_metrics.description: Reject claims under 35 U.S.C. 102(a)(2) as anticipated by a U.S. patent, U.S. patent application publication, or WIPO publication with an earlier effective filing date; the reference need not have a common assignee or inventor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used for applications filed on/after March 16, 2013 (precede with 7.03.aia). 102(a)(2) may be applied if the reference is (a) U.S. patent under 151 with earlier effective filing date, (b) U.S. patent application publication under 122(b) with earlier effective filing date, or (c) WIPO PCT publication/designating international design application with earlier effective filing date. If any of the three types was published before the claimed effective filing date, it is also applicable under 102(a)(1). Insert claim numbers, indicate 'clearly anticipated' or 'anticipated' and provide explanation and prior art. Precede by 7.12.aia.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rejection for Public Use, On Sale, or Other Public Availability (35 U.S.C. 102(a)(1) / pre‑AIA 102(b)) (7.16.aia / 7.16.fti)
rubrics_metrics.description: Reject claims based on public use, sale, or other public availability of the invention under 35 U.S.C. 102(a)(1) (AIA) or pre‑AIA 102(b) as appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For AIA (7.16.aia) use in applications filed on/after March 16, 2013 (precede with 7.03.aia and 7.07.aia/7.08.aia or 7.103). For pre‑AIA (7.16.fti) precede with 7.07.fti and 7.09.fti or 7.103. Must provide a full explanation of the evidence establishing public use or sale in the bracketed explanation. For situations where a reference was disqualified under 102(b)(2)(C) but still applies under 102(a)(1), see 7.17.aia.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of Prior Art Excepted Under 102(b)(2)(C) as Prior Art Under 102(a)(1) (7.17.aia)
rubrics_metrics.description: When a reference has been disqualified as prior art under 35 U.S.C. 102(a)(2) due to exceptions (e.g., common ownership or joint research agreement) but still qualifies as prior art under 35 U.S.C. 102(a)(1), the examiner may reject under 102(a)(1).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Inform applicant which entity established ownership/joint research agreement and identify the disqualified reference. Applicant may overcome the 102(a)(1) rejection by relying on exceptions under 102(b)(1)(A) (showing under 37 CFR 1.130(a) that the subject matter was obtained from the inventor/joint inventor) or 102(b)(1)(B) (evidence of prior public disclosure via affidavit/declaration under 37 CFR 1.130(b)). This form is used for applications filed on/after March 16, 2013 and must be preceded by 7.03.aia; precede by 7.07.aia and 7.08.aia or 7.103; include claim numbers and full explanation of evidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rejection for Abandonment of Invention (Pre‑AIA 35 U.S.C. 102(c)) (7.17.fti)
rubrics_metrics.description: Reject claims under pre‑AIA 35 U.S.C. 102(c) where the invention has been abandoned.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This form paragraph must be preceded by form paragraphs 7.07.fti and 7.10.fti or by 7.103. In the bracketed explanation, insert a full explanation of the evidence establishing abandonment (see MPEP § 2134).
